title: The Untranslatable Remainder
text:
Every literary translation involves a loss that no skill can entirely prevent. The translator must choose between preserving the literal sense of a sentence and recreating its rhythm, ambiguity and cultural resonance. Scholars have long debated whether this remainder is a failure or the very condition that makes translation a creative act.

A celebrated example concerns poetic wordplay, where a pun that delights in the source language may become flat or incomprehensible in another. Rather than abandon the joke, a skilful translator often relocates the effect, substituting a different pun that produces a comparable response in the new reader. Such compensation demonstrates that fidelity lies less in individual words than in the effect the text produces.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must a translator choose between?
options: Publishing the text or leaving it unpublished
Preserving the literal sense or recreating rhythm, ambiguity and cultural resonance

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what may happen to a pun when it is moved into another language?
options: It becomes longer than the original
It may become flat or incomprehensible
It is always removed by the publisher
It is translated word for word without loss

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the remainder that scholars have debated?
options: It can be eliminated entirely with enough skill
It may be an inherent part of what makes translation a creative act
It is evidence that translators are careless
It appears only in prose, never in poetry

questions.text: The passage implies that a translator who substitutes a different pun is most concerned with:
options: Matching the exact words of the original
Producing a comparable response in the new reader
Reducing the length of the translated text
Explaining the joke in a footnote

vocabulary.definition: the part that is left over after everything else has been removed or accounted for
the quality of having more than one possible meaning
a joke that exploits two meanings of a word or similar-sounding words
something that makes up for a loss or a lack elsewhere

paragraph_translations: Toda traducción literaria implica una pérdida que ninguna habilidad puede evitar por completo. El traductor debe elegir entre conservar el sentido literal de una frase y recrear su ritmo, su ambigüedad y su resonancia cultural. Los estudiosos han debatido durante mucho tiempo si ese remanente es un fracaso o la condición misma que convierte la traducción en un acto creativo.

Un ejemplo célebre se refiere al juego verbal poético, donde un juego de palabras que deleita en la lengua original puede volverse plano o incomprensible en otra. En lugar de renunciar al chiste, un traductor hábil suele trasladar el efecto, sustituyendo por otro juego de palabras que provoque una respuesta comparable en el nuevo lector. Tal compensación demuestra que la fidelidad reside menos en las palabras individuales que en el efecto que produce el texto.
